About Event

​About Event

​Welcome to the Post-Training & RL Buildathon — a one-day, in-person gathering in San Francisco for engineers, AI builders, founders, and researchers who want to spend a full day building with post-training techniques: SFT, RLHF/RLAIF, DPO/GRPO, reward modeling, RL environments, evals, and agentic fine-tuning.

​Hosted by Devnovate in collaboration with AWS, the day pairs hands-on building with a panel of practitioners from fast-growing AI companies who are putting RL and post-training into production.

​Event Details

​When: 9:30 AM – 7:00 PM, Thursday, 30 October 2026

​Where: San Francisco, CA

​Format: One-day in-person buildathon + practitioner panel

​Who: ML engineers, AI builders, founders, researchers, data scientists, and technology professionals

​Theme: Post-training & reinforcement learning

​What to Expect

​A full day dedicated to building on post-training and RL

​Panel: “RL in Production” with engineers from TinyFish, and other leading AWS customers

​Mentorship from experienced ML practitioners and AWS solution architects

​AWS credits, partner credits, and challenge prizes

​Access to modern AI tools, APIs, GPUs, and developer resources

​Live demos and project showcases at the end of the day

​Food, refreshments, swag, and prizes

​What Can You Build?
Anything that uses post-training or RL to make a model or agent better:

​Fine-tune an open-weight model on a domain dataset (SFT DPO GRPO)

​Build a reward model or RL environment for an agentic task

​Train an agent with RL to use tools, browse, or complete multi-step workflows

​Design evals and preference datasets for alignment or task performance

​Optimize inference-time behavior with learned policies

​Or something nobody has tried before

​Bring an idea, a dataset, a model you want to improve — or just the desire to build. Find teammates, get feedback, and ship something real by the end of the day.

​Who Should Join?
Whether you’re an ML engineer shipping fine-tuned models, a researcher exploring RL for agents, a founder testing an AI product, or a student getting into post-training — you’re welcome. You don’t need to be an expert. You just need to be ready to build.

​Come with a model. Leave with a better one.

About Event

Join top AI engineers, founders, and builders at the AWS Builder Loft in San Francisco for a full day of building production-ready AI agents powered by live web data.
Special Halloween themed tracks and Best Costume Prize
Build on You.com developer platform, Parasail, One, and Crewai and collaborate directly with the engineers behind the APIs to ship something real and SPOOKY in a single day.
Why Attend?
Build alongside Bay Area's top AI engineers, founders, and builders

Learn directly from You.com 's product and engineering leaders

Get hands-on help from the engineers behind the APIs powering Agentic Era

Ship a working prototype in one day and demo your project to AI leaders and judges

Expand your network with some of the Bay Area's best

Themes
🧟 Theme 1: "The Exorcism Protocol" (Autonomous Agent Swarms)
A paranormal outbreak is spreading through a live facility simulation. Teams build an autonomous supervised swarm — CrewAI agents with distinct roles, tools, and only partial individual knowledge — that must sense, share intel, and coordinate containment in real time. Victory is measured by the swarm, not a single model: containment speed, false-alarm rate, and "civilians saved" all feed the live venue scoreboard.
🎃 Theme 2: The "Haunted Dashboard" (Generative UI Pipelines)
Create an automated Spooky Tactical Command Station served by Parasail's inference endpoints. The system takes real-time, unstructured "Spooky Incident Logs" (e.g., zombie outbreaks, phantom activity levels) and processes them through a structured retrieval network to dynamically build and compile functional, beautifully designed web interfaces on the fly over WebSockets.
Prizes
The top teams compete for a stacked prize pool of $10k+ from You.com and our partners.

AI and machine-learning engineers

Software engineers building with LLMs and agents

About Us

You.com is the leading AI search infrastructure — built for developers. Our APIs let you build intelligent agents and applications that use live, factual data from the web, news, and research, in real time. With just a few lines of code, you can power your LLMs with up-to-date, citation-backed results instead of static training data.
One ( withone.ai ) provides managed auth and 729 platform integrations behind a four-command CLI, plus agent memory, scheduling, and webhooks. Load-bearing partner for the theme. Track 1 does not exist without it. Contact: Edward Irby.
CrewAI provides multi-agent orchestration and is the default framework in the starter repo. Repeat partner from SF, where they supplied credits and an on-site engineer.
Parasail is an AI inference cloud that lets companies run and scale AI models on GPUs from a global network without owning or managing hardware. Its orchestration engine sends each workload to available GPUs
AWS is Amazon’s cloud platform, offering on-demand computing, storage, databases, networking and AI/ML services that companies of all sizes use to build and run applications without managing their own data centers.
UpScaleX is a pre-seed to seed fund co-building with technically strong founders across the AI stack, from AI infrastructure to applications. We support founders from day one with capital, hands-on product and GTM work, and a network of 10,000+ innovators

About Event

Registrations open!
Build it. Code it. Put it to the test.
Forget everything you know about a traditional hackathon. This is one day, two tracks, and a whole lot of hardware.
Pick your challenge, build something real, and spend the day working alongside Qualcomm engineers and mentors who will help you take your project from idea to working demo.
Choose Your Track
⚽ Track 1: Train a Robot to Score
Your challenge: take a Qualcomm-powered robocar and teach it to see, navigate, find the goal, and score autonomously .
Using our Robot Soccer Cup resources, you'll work with robotics, computer vision, and on-device AI to train your robocar to complete the challenge entirely on its own.
There are no 1:1 matches this time. Instead, every team gets the same mission:
Which robocar can identify the goal and score first?
You'll have the day to build, tune, test, break things, fix them, and make your robot faster and smarter before putting it through the final challenge.
🕹️ Track 2: Build Your Own Arcade Game
Prefer building something you can play?
Grab an Arduino UNO Q Arcade Bundle and build your own arcade game from scratch.
You'll work with the UNO Q hardware and turn your idea into a playable experience by the end of the day. Make it nostalgic, competitive, weird, chaotic — that's entirely up to you.
What's in it for you?
🛠️ Real hands-on build time with hardware, AI, robotics, or game development — not slides, not theory

🤖 Two completely different tracks depending on what you want to explore

🤝 A full day with Qualcomm mentors and engineers on-site to help you troubleshoot, experiment, and keep building

📄 A project you can actually talk about on your resume, portfolio, or in interviews

🎒 No prior robotics or hardware experience required — we'll give you the resources you need to get started

🧰 All hardware provided by Qualcomm for both tracks

Before the Event
We don't want your first hour at the event to be spent figuring out where to start.
Qualcomm will provide Developer Journey Guides for both tracks so you can familiarize yourself with the hardware, tools, and challenge ahead of time.
We'll also host office hours before the event , giving you a chance to meet the mentors, ask questions, get your development environment ready, and make sure you're set up for success before the big day.
On event day, Qualcomm mentors will be available on-site throughout the entire experience to answer questions, help debug problems, and keep your project moving.
Step 1: Register on Luma today (Space is limited!)
Step 2: Check your Northeastern Email for a pre-event resources and updates
Step 3: Honor your spot + commitment by showing up and participating (or let us know if you can't make it so we can prepare accordingly)
Step 4: Remember to update your career capital (resume, LinkedIn, portfolios) with what you learned and built from this workshop!

Mackenzie Room

Registration

Welcome! To join the event, please register below.
Register

About Event

Satellite imagery is data, and you can work with it. In this in-person workshop, Stace Maples of the Stanford Geospatial Center shows you how to get started with Earth observation data and tools.
What we will cover
A Tiny Introduction to Remote Sensing: what makes data spatial, how vector and raster data differ, and how pixels in satellite imagery store measurements of the Earth's surface

Account setup: we add you to the Geospatial Center's Earth Engine Google Cloud organization and help you register your project as non-commercial

A quick introduction to the Earth Engine Code Editor

A demo of the Earth Engine Python API in a notebook

Planet.com : we use results from the notebook demo to learn how to search Planet's satellite imagery

When to use Earth Engine, when to use Planet, and how they work together

No GIS, remote sensing, or spatial data experience is required. Bring a laptop to follow along.
Who should attend: Stanford students, faculty, researchers, and staff, including GreenAI Hackathon participants.
Presented by: Stace Maples (Stanford Geospatial Center, Stanford Libraries)
